title: Builder-Vite: Centralize Vite plugins for builder-vite and addon-vitest
body:
Closes https://github.com/storybookjs/storybook/issues/33813

<!-- If your PR is related to an issue, provide the number(s) above; if it resolves multiple issues, be sure to break them up (e.g. "closes #1000, closes #1001"). -->

<!--

Thank you for contributing to Storybook! Please submit all PRs to the `next` branch unless they are specific to the current release. Storybook maintainers cherry-pick bug and documentation fixes into the `main` branch as part of the release process, so you shouldn't need to worry about this. For additional guidance: https://storybook.js.org/docs/contribute

-->

## What I did

This PR refactors the @storybook/builder-vite plugin architecture to move core logic into a more modular, plugin-based structure.

### Key Changes
**1. Modularization of Vite Plugins**
Previously, much of the Vite configuration (resolve conditions, environment variables, fs-allow rules) was hardcoded within the builder's vite-config.ts. These have been extracted into self-contained plugins:

- `storybookConfigPlugin`: Handles resolve conditions (storybook, stories, test), envPrefix (VITE_, STORYBOOK_), and filesystem access.
- `storybookProjectAnnotationsPlugin`: Manages the virtual module for composed project annotations (getProjectAnnotations).
- `storybookRuntimePlugin`: Handles external globals and environment variable injection.

**2. Introduction of viteCorePlugins Preset**
A new `viteCorePlugins` preset has been added to builder-vite/src/preset.ts. (We don't want to use `viteFinal` to be able to clearly distinguish what is a shareable core plugin and what is config contributed by other addons/frameworks/user config - This was requested by Jeppe). This serves as the single source of truth for the Vite setup required to run Storybook code, and it can now be applied by both the standard builder and the addon-vitest.

**3. Refined Virtual Module Handling**
The project annotations logic has been moved out of the monolithic `codeGeneratorPlugin` into a dedicated virtual `module: virtual:/@storybook/builder-vite/project-annotations.js`. This allows tests and external tools to access composed annotations. The project annotations will be re-used in `@storybook/addon-vitest` in SB 11, since it is considered a breaking change because it might conflict with the user's existing `.storybook/vitest.setup.ts` file.

**4. Cleanups and Optimization**
- Removed sanitizeEnvVars in favor of the new storybookRuntimePlugin, which handles define injection via the standard Vite plugin config hook.
- Dependency Optimization: Simplified getOptimizeDeps logic and moved it into a plugin-driven approach.

**Impact on @storybook/addon-vitest**
By leveraging the new `viteCorePlugins` preset, addon-vitest can now automatically stay in sync with the builder's configuration for resolve conditions, globals, and docgen, reducing the maintenance burden and preventing configuration drift.

**Weak hash function can produce collisions.**

This hash function sums character codes, so permutations of the same characters produce identical hashes (e.g., `"abc"` and `"cba"` both hash to 294). While the filename prefix provides some disambiguation, consider a more robust approach if uniqueness is important.

<details>
<summary>🔧 Suggested improvement using a simple string hash</summary>

```diff
 function hash(value: string) {
-  return value.split('').reduce((acc, char) => acc + char.charCodeAt(0), 0);
+  // Simple djb2-style hash for better distribution
+  return value.split('').reduce((acc, char) => ((acc << 5) - acc + char.charCodeAt(0)) | 0, 5381) >>> 0;
 }
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
In `@code/builders/builder-vite/src/codegen-project-annotations.ts` around lines
95 - 97, The current hash function (hash) in codegen-project-annotations.ts is
weak (sums char codes) and can collide for permutations; replace it with a
robust deterministic string hash (e.g., FNV-1a or a cryptographic hash like
SHA-1/SHA-256 via crypto.createHash) so returned values are hex digests rather
than simple integers, and update any callers expecting the old numeric value to
accept the new string digest; ensure the implementation remains deterministic
and performant for filenames and adjust tests if they assert the previous
numeric output.
```

</details>

**Remove the `Promise` wrapper from the generic parameter in `presets.apply`.**

The code currently uses `presets.apply<Promise<Builder_EnvsRaw>>('env')`, which causes double-Promise typing. Since `apply<T>` returns `Promise<T>`, this results in `Promise<Promise<Builder_EnvsRaw>>`. After awaiting, `envs` remains a Promise instead of the object, causing `Object.keys(envs)` and `stringifyProcessEnvs(envs, ...)` to fail at runtime.

Other usages in the codebase correctly apply the pattern with `presets.apply<Record<string, string>>('env')` (see `common-preset.ts` lines 145, 155 and `builder-webpack5` line 65).

<details>
<summary>Correct usage</summary>

```diff
-  const envs = await options.presets.apply<Promise<Builder_EnvsRaw>>('env');
+  const envs = await options.presets.apply<Builder_EnvsRaw>('env');
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
In `@code/builders/builder-vite/src/plugins/storybook-runtime-plugin.ts` around
lines 57 - 66, In storybookRuntimePlugin, presets.apply is incorrectly typed as
presets.apply<Promise<Builder_EnvsRaw>>('env') causing a double Promise so
awaited envs is still a Promise; change the generic to the raw type (e.g.,
presets.apply<Builder_EnvsRaw>('env') or
presets.apply<Record<string,string>>('env')) so await returns the actual env
object, then stringifyProcessEnvs(envs, config.envPrefix) and Object.keys(envs)
will operate on the real object; update the call site in storybookRuntimePlugin
and ensure the envs variable usage (stringifyProcessEnvs, Object.keys) assumes
the non-Promise shape.
```

</details>

**Unused `existing` parameter and misleading JSDoc about included plugins.**

The `existing` parameter is declared but never used. Both call sites pass an empty array (`[]`), and the function doesn't reference it anywhere in the body. Additionally, the JSDoc (lines 22-23) mentions "Docgen plugin" and "Runtime plugin" as included features, but they are not returned by this function—they are added separately in `vite-config.ts` (lines 77-78) and `vitest-plugin/index.ts`. The JSDoc should be corrected to accurately describe only what `viteCorePlugins` actually returns, and the unused parameter should either be removed or used as intended.

<details>
<summary>🐛 Proposed fix to remove unused parameter</summary>

```diff
 export async function viteCorePlugins(
-  existing: PluginOption[],
   options: Options
 ): Promise<PluginOption[]> {
```

```diff

- * - **Docgen plugin**: CSF processing and component metadata extraction
- * - **Runtime plugin**: External globals transformation for pre-bundled Storybook modules
  * - **Mocking plugins**: Injects the mocker runtime script into the HTML and sets up rules to swap
  *   modules based on sb.mock() calls.
```

💡 Result:

### What `optimizeDeps.entries` does (and why plugins should be careful)

- **Default behavior (when `optimizeDeps.entries` is _unset_)**: Vite scans/crawls your project’s entry HTML files to discover imports that should be pre-bundled (or uses `build.rollupOptions.input` if set). [1]
- **When `optimizeDeps.entries` is explicitly set**: it **overwrites default entry inference**—Vite will scan only the provided glob(s) (relative to project root). [1]
- **Ignore semantics change when you set it**: with explicit `entries`, by default only `node_modules` and `build.outDir` are ignored; other ignores must be expressed via `!` patterns. Also, `node_modules` is **not ignored** if your pattern explicitly includes `node_modules`. [1]
- **Best practice implied by Vite docs**: if dependency discovery works without forcing entries, it’s generally better **not** to set/force extra scanning knobs, to avoid unnecessary work and let the browser handle more requests in parallel. [2]

### How config merging affects plugins that “add entries”

In a plugin’s `config` hook, returning a partial config is **deep-merged**, and direct mutation is supported when merge behavior isn’t what you need. [3] Vite’s config merging utilities generally **concatenate arrays** for many fields, which can make “I’ll just append my entry” behave differently than expected (e.g., turning a string into an array or producing unexpected unions). [4]

### Practical best practices for plugins

1. **Prefer not touching `optimizeDeps.entries` at all** unless you have a concrete failure mode that requires it (e.g., you generate “virtual” entry-like files that Vite can’t discover otherwise). This avoids overriding user intent and changing ignore semantics. [1]
2. **Never blindly set `optimizeDeps.entries`** (because it disables default inference). If you must, **only do so when the user hasn’t set it**.
3. **If you need additive behavior, compute it explicitly** instead of relying on deep-merge array concatenation:
   - read existing `config.optimizeDeps?.entries`
   - normalize to an array
   - add your patterns if missing
   - assign back (mutation is acceptable here). [3]
4. **Document the tradeoffs**: setting entries changes what gets crawled and how ignores work, so users should know why your plugin is doing it and how to override/disable it. [1]

### Safe pattern (plugin skeleton)

```ts
export default function myPlugin() {
  return {
    name: 'my-plugin',
    config(config) {
      const od = (config.optimizeDeps ??= {})

      // Respect user config: only provide entries if user did not set them.
      if (od.entries == null) {
        od.entries = ['index.html'] // or your specific glob(s)
        return
      }

      // If you truly need to add entries, do it explicitly (avoid merge surprises).
      const existing = Array.isArray(od.entries) ? od.entries : [od.entries]
      const extra = 'path/to/generated/**/*.html'
      if (!existing.includes(extra)) od.entries = [...existing, extra]
    },
  }
}
```
